articles.title: IPL COO Amin, IOA CEO Iyer in Sports Ministry committee to create framework for leagues in India - Sportstar
articles.summary: IPL COO Amin, IOA CEO Iyer in Sports Ministry committee to create framework for leagues in India Sportstar
articles.content: New Delhi The Sports Ministry on Wednesday formed a 14-member committee to formulate a framework for developing “professionally managed and financially sustainable” leagues in India, with BCCI CEO and IPL COO Hemang Amin among the prominent members of the panel. The committee, which also includes IOA CEO Raghuram Iyer, has been mandated to assess existing ecosystem “constraints” and identify priority sports. It would be required to recommend measures to attract corporate capital, franchise ownership, sponsorships, broadcasting and digital rights, and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) financing. Empowered to consult National Sports Federations, existing league officials, investors, and sports technology firms, the committee has been given eight weeks to submit its final recommendations to the Ministry “While several sports leagues in the country have achieved varying levels of success, many disciplines with strong sporting and social potential face commercial viability hurdles during their initial stages,” the ministry said in a statement. “Accordingly, the Committee will assess the present sports league ecosystem to identify the major issues and constraints affecting the establishment and sustainability of leagues...(the committee) will identify priority sports and categories, particularly Olympic sports, women’s sports, youth sports, indigenous sports, and emerging sports, to recommend suitable operational models tailored to their sporting and commercial potential,” it added. ALSO READ | Murali Sreeshankar: Why should asking for fair financial recognition be seen as greed? https://sportstar.thehindu.com/athletics/indian-athletes-prize-money-financial-security-state-rewards-murali-sreeshankar-column/article71714877.ece The panel also includes top Sports Ministry officials Kunal, Joint Secretary (Governance), who will be its convener, and Vineel Krishna, Joint Secretary (Khelo India), along with representatives from major broadcasters like JioStar, Sony Network, Doordarshan, and Zee Network. The panel’s formation is a major step towards Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya’s stated goal of creating a robust league system in India. Currently, the leagues that have managed to capture the attention of fans include the IPL at the very top, followed by franchise-based leagues in badminton, kabaddi, hockey and wrestling, among others. However, almost all of them have battled financial issues, with the hockey league facing the prospect of a shutdown within two years of its revival. The Indian Super League and the Indian Women’s League — the country’s top tiers for men’s and women’s football — have also faced significant delays in the past due to commercial rights issues and scheduling problems. Meanwhile, the Pro Kabaddi League is currently in a state of limbo due to uncertainty over broadcast rights. The Ministry said a league ecosystem would not just help talent but would also bring in private investment and generate employment across sports management, broadcasting, technology, and events. “...the Committee will examine mechanisms for structured Government facilitation alongside active participation from the private sector, sports organisations, State Governments, local bodies, and communities. This includes evaluating targeted interventions such as Viability Gap Funding (a one-time government grant to infrastructure projects), direct and indirect financial assistance, and concessional access to Government sports infrastructure,” the Ministry stated. Additionally, the committee will propose strategies to integrate leagues with schools, colleges, universities, and local clubs to “foster grassroots participation”. The composition of the Committee Kunal, Joint Secretary (Governance) Convener, Vineel Krishna, (Joint Secretary -Khelo India), Raghuram Iyer (CEO, IOA, B Srinivasan (RIL), Hemang Amin (BCCI CEO and COO IPL), P.K.S.V. Sagar (GMR Sports), Sanjay Adesara (Adani Sportsline), Divyanshu Singh (JSW Sports), Ishan Chatterjee (Jio Hotstar), Rajesh Kaul (Sony Pictures), Anupam Swaroop (DD Sports), Parag Darade (Zee Entertainment), Abhijit Bhattacharya (BVL), Advocate Nandan Kamath. articles.summary: Maharashtra declares four more talukas drought-hit; total rises to 308 The Hindu
articles.content: Mumbai Maharashtra government has declared four more talukas as drought affected areas, bringing the total to 308 out of 358 talukas. The four newly added talukas are Chiplun, Wada and Vikramgad in Konkan, and Dindori in Nashik district, whereas nine other talukas, including Hatkanangale,, Karveer and Gadhinglaj in Kolhapur district, and Pen and Mahad from Raigad are been assessed for the drought situation. Konkan region annually receives the highest rainfall. Drought-stricken Beed: Land of parched fields and broken promises Drought-stricken Beed: Land of parched fields and broken promises Drought has devastated Maharashtra’s Beed district, pushing women farmers and labourers towards distress migration. Despite repeated pleas for employment, villagers say government job guarantees have failed them, even as the State announces a ₹6,728-crore package SPOTLIGHT Drought-stricken Beed: Land of parched fields and broken promises storyline 1 The announcement came on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), when Revenue Minister and chairman of the cabinet sub-committee on drought relief, Chandrashekhar Bawankule, said, “The four talukas were added after members at the meeting brought to notice the water scarcity and crop losses faced by farmers in these regions. 13 such proposals were made, four talukas were added to list.” The state government in October added 40 talukas to the first list of 265 talukas drought-hit, the total rose to 305. Trigger 1 and Trigger 2 have been applied in these talukas, making them eligible for assistance under the Centre’s National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) guidelines. The measures include a complete waiver of examination fees for students in drought-hit talukas, without any eligibility criteria. Maharashtra sets up drought mitigation panel, approves ₹291.91 crore relief for flood-hit farmers Maharashtra sets up drought mitigation panel, approves ₹291.91 crore relief for flood-hit farmers The measures follow deficient rainfall in parts of Maharashtra during 2026, prompting the government to declare drought in talukas identified under the Kharif season’s Trigger-1 assessment Maharashtra sets up drought mitigation panel, approves ₹291.91 crore relief for flood-hit farmers storyline 1 At the drought committee meeting, financial assistance for farmers was also discussed. So far, ₹4,701.6 crore has been distributed to 94.3 lakh farmers across the State, as per the Agriculture Department. Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar division received the highest assistance of ₹1,704.5 crore, then Nashik ₹1,001.2 crore and others.

articles.title: Sporting spirit shines as Pakistan give India guard of honour after SAFF final - India Today
articles.summary: Sporting spirit shines as Pakistan give India guard of honour after SAFF final India Today
articles.content: In a sporting rivalry increasingly defined by the absence of handshakes, Indian and Pakistani footballers offered a reminder that competition need not come at the cost of camaraderie. After India defeated Pakistan 2-1 in the SAFF Championship final in Dhaka on Tuesday, the Pakistani players lined up to give the newly crowned champions a guard of honour, providing a striking contrast to the strained sporting exchanges between the neighbouring countries in recent times.The gesture stood out against the backdrop of the no-handshake policy that has become a feature of India-Pakistan cricket encounters since the 2025 Asia Cup. The two cricket teams have repeatedly avoided customary greetings, both at the toss and after matches, with the practice extending to the men's and women's teams across competitions.The trend began after the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025 and the subsequent military escalation between the two countries. It continued through the 2025 Asia Cup, the Under-19 Asia Cup, the Women's World Cup and the Women's Asia Cup in 2026. Even at the Asian Games in Japan last month, India captain Shreyas Iyer and Pakistan skipper Sahibzada Farhan did not shake hands at the toss before the men's cricket final.Football, however, offered a different picture.The final in Dhaka was not the first instance of the two teams exchanging pleasantries during the tournament. Before their group-stage meeting on November 5, India head coach Naushad Moosa had indicated that his players would follow customary pre-match greetings. India captain Bijoy Varghese subsequently shook hands with Pakistan skipper Yousuf Ijaz Butt.The post-final scenes offered another illustration of that sporting spirit, with players from both sides exchanging handshakes and high-fives during the medal ceremony. Pakistan's guard of honour for the Indian champions was a particularly memorable moment after a fiercely contested final.The contrast was also visible at the Asian Games, where Indian and Pakistani athletes across hockey, volleyball, table tennis and squash exchanged greetings despite the strained relations between the countries. India's hockey players and their Pakistani counterparts shook hands after a dramatic semifinal, while Pakistani volleyball players were seen consoling Indian opponents after a victory.On the pitch, India had to fight back from a goal down to secure their 10th SAFF Championship title and complete a hat-trick of consecutive triumphs.Pakistan, appearing in their maiden SAFF final, took the lead through Alamgir Ghazi in first-half stoppage time, catching India off guard. The Blue Tigers struggled to find their rhythm in the opening period but were handed an advantage when Junaid Shah was sent off in the 59th minute following a VAR review for a dangerous challenge on Brison Fernandes.India made their numerical advantage count. Suhail Ahmad Bhat restored parity in the 60th minute before Sandip Mandi struck an 88th-minute winner to complete the comeback.The 2026 SAFF Championship, the premier men's football competition for South Asian national teams, featured six countries. India sent a second-string squad comprising predominantly younger players under U-23 coach Naushad Moosa, rather than its first-choice senior team.- Ends

articles.summary: Indian sports wrap, November 17: Tanay, Sneha upset seeds, reach third round at Junior Badminton Nationals The Hindu
articles.content: CHENNAI BADMINTON Tanay, Sneha upset seeds, reach third round at Junior Badminton Nationals Rajasthan’s Sneha Lamba and Maharashtra’s Tanay Mehendale created early flutter in the 49th National Junior (U-19) badminton championships in Gangtok on Tuesday with straight-games upsets of much higher-ranked opponents. In girls’ singles, Sneha won 15-12, 15-6 against fourth seed Tanvi Reddy Andluri, who recently represented India in the World Junior Championships in Cairo, Egypt, while Tanay got the better of sixth seed Shaurya Mishra 15-13, 16-14 in boys’ singles. The seeds had got a bye in the opening round and all eyes were on the top stars to deliver on the second day of the individual competitions in Sikkim’s capital. While women’s top seed Shaina Manimuthu was pushed to three games by Maharashtra’s Naishaa Kaur Bhatoye, the Karnataka shuttler kept her nerves to win 15-9, 11-15, 15-5. Nishchal Anand, the top seed in boys’ singles, was also made to dig deep to beat Prangan Choudhury 15-11, 14-16, 15-10 in the second round. However, 11th and 13th seeds in boys’ singles were shown the door. Eleventh-seeded Sai Nachiketh Bhatraju lost 15-10, 9-15, 15-12 to Prince while 13th-seeded Harshad Shadish bowed out after a 15-12, 13-15, 15-9 defeat against Sparsh Sood. - Team Sportstar CRICKET Pakistan beats India by one wicket in last-ball thriller at Asia Cup Cricket for the Blind The much-anticipated India-Pakistan clash at the Asia Cup Cricket for the Blind 2026 lived up to its billing, producing a nail-biting finish as Pakistan secured a dramatic one-wicket victory off the final ball of the contest at Bashundhara Sports City, Dhaka. In a match that swung between the two sides, Pakistan chased down India’s challenging total of 179/6, finishing at 180/9 in 20 overs. - Team Sportstar ESPORTS Vanshaj Sharma wins Red Bull Wings Cup India, qualifies for World Final in Miami Vanshaj Sharma was crowned the Red Bull Wings Cup India National Champion after defeating Saransh Jain 2–0 in the best-of-three final at a packed Kettle Studio in Bengaluru on Sunday. The victory secured Sharma’s place at the Red Bull Wings Cup World Final in Miami, where he will represent India against national champions from around the world. Sharma won the opening game of the EA SPORTS FC 27 final 5–1 before sealing the title with a 4–1 victory in the second game. The straight-games result capped a dominant run through the eight-player knockout tournament, with Sharma winning all four games he played across the quarterfinals, semifinals and final. His campaign began with a 6–0 quarterfinal victory over Sharuk Sanjay. He followed that with a 10–2 win against Fadl Afridi in the semifinals, his highest-scoring performance of the evening, to book his place in the title decider. Across the tournament, Sharma scored 25 goals and conceded just four. Jain reached the final from the other half of the bracket, opening with a 9–2 win over Dhruv Keshwani before edging Rohit J Abraham 3–2 in the semifinals. His narrow semifinal victory set up the meeting with Sharma, who carried his scoring form into the championship contest and closed out the series without needing a third game. The remaining quarterfinals saw Rohit J Abraham defeat Satyam Jha 3–1, while Fadl Afridi progressed with a 4–0 victory over Akshay S. An exhibition clash between GodLike and Apex Gaming added another contest to the evening. Dobby and SMR represented GodLike, while Jonathan teamed up with Hydro for Apex Gaming. The Apex duo secured a comfortable 10–3 victory in the showmatch, which brought the two organisations together on the virtual football pitch. - Team Sportstar GOLF Ridhima takes lead in 15th Leg of WPGT, amateur Aida tied third with Vani and Tvesa Ridhima Dilawari made a confident start, carding a two-under 69 to take the opening-round lead at the 15th and final leg of the Women’s Pro Golf Tour at the Jaypee Wishtown Golf Course in Noida on Tuesday. Riya Jadon was just one stroke behind with a one-under 70, while amateur Aida Thimmaiah joined experienced professionals Vani Kapoor and Tvesa Malik at even-par 71. The opening round proved a demanding test for the field. Only two players managed under par scores, while three others returned even-par cards. The leader of the Order of Merit, Dilawari, continued to impress by picking up four birdies against two bogeys. Her four victories this year came at Kalhaar Blues & Greens, Poona Club, Jaypee Wishtown and Prestige Golfshire. She has also finished runner-up twice. She finished third in the 14th leg last week at the Rambagh Golf Club event behind the winner Jasmine Shekar and runner-up Vani. Jasmine has skipped the event as she is one of the six Indians playing in a Q-School event in Thailand. One of the encouraging performances of the day came from Bengaluru amateur golfer Aida, who had three birdies and three bogeys and on two occasions on the back nine she picked a birdie and immediately gave back the shot on the very next hole. Tvesa also finished at even par, although her round followed the opposite pattern. She was three-under 33 on the front nine including three birdies in a row from the seventh. She dropped three strokes on the back nine without any birdies to sign for 71. Tvesa has had a productive recent spell, finishing seventh at the Hero Women’s Indian Open with a one-under total of 287 (71-73-71-72). She has also recorded a domestic tour victory this season. Saanvi Somu, Lavanya Jadon and Sneha Singh were tied sixth at 1-over 72 and as many as nine players were tied for ninth place. The huge bunch included Shrestha Shukla, Mannat Brar, Prarthana Khanna, Shweta Mansingh, Jasmandeep Kaur, Yaalisai Verma, Sneha Sharan, Janneya Dasanniee and Agrima Manral. - PTI Saurav Rathi shoots 65 to take opening-round lead at Servo Masters Gurugram’s Saurav Rathi opened the new DP World PGTI season with a bang, firing an impressive seven-under 65 to take a two-shot lead after the first round of the Rs 1 crore IndianOil SERVO Masters Golf in Digboi, Assam, on Tuesday. Rathi, 24, made eight birdies and dropped his only shot on the par-4 18th, his closing hole, to emerge as the outright leader on a course where only 29 players in the 120-man field managed to break par. Delhi’s 21-year-old Anshul Kabthiyal and seasoned campaigner Om Prakash Chouhan shared second place at five-under 67. Rathi, a regular on the DP World PGTI since 2019, recently secured his full playing rights for the new season after finishing 17th at the DP World PGTI Qualifying Tournament Final Stage in Ahmedabad. Despite nursing a left-leg injury sustained after slipping on wet stairs at the course on Monday, Rathi hit 12 of 14 fairways and 15 greens in regulation. “It was a solid round and a good start to the new season. I was five-under after nine holes, made two more birdies on the 11th and 12th, followed by another birdie on the 14th. I made pars after that before dropping a disappointing bogey on the 18th from the middle of the fairway, just 40 yards out,” said Rathi. Chouhan, an 11-time winner on the DP World PGTI, a former winner on the European Challenge Tour and the 2023 DP World PGTI rankings champion, also carded a 67, making eight birdies against three bogeys. Four players shared fourth place at four-under 68, including Gurugram’s Kushal Singh, Pune’s Divyansh Dubey, Kapurthala’s Yuvraj Singh and Lucknow’s Sanjeev Kumar. Kushal made seven birdies and three bogeys, while Divyansh registered six birdies and two bogeys. Yuvraj recovered from a double-bogey on the par-5 15th and another bogey with seven birdies, while Sanjeev produced five birdies against a lone bogey. - PTI SQUASH Senthilkumar in Qatar squash semifinals Indian squash player Velavan Senthilkumar moved into the semifinals of the QSF 3 PSA Copper tournament with a straight-game victory over Egypt’s Omar Said in Doha, Qatar, on Tuesday. Second seed Senthilkumar, who won two PSA Copper-level titles this year, beat his fifth-seeded opponent 11-9, 11-1, 13-11 in the quarterfinals of the USD 40,500 prize money tournament for men. World No 38 Senthilkumar will next meet the winner of the quarterfinal between local challenger Abdulla Al-Tamimi and Malaysia’s Ameeshenraj Chandaran. -Team Sportstar

articles.title: Maharashtra approves Rs 16.74 crore VGF for Sindhudurg-Navi Mumbai flights - PSU Watch
articles.summary: Maharashtra approves Rs 16.74 crore VGF for Sindhudurg-Navi Mumbai flights PSU Watch
articles.content: New Delhi: The Maharashtra Government has approved Rs 16.74 crore in Viability Gap Funding (VGF) to run flights between Sindhudurg and Navi Mumbai for a year, replacing an earlier plan to link the coastal Konkan district with Mumbai airport, officials said..Follow The PSUWatch Channel on Whatsapp.To revive air services from Chipi airport in Sindhudurg district, known for its scenic shoreline, historic forts and lush green Western Ghats, the state cabinet on October 27 gave nod to 100 percent VGF for airlines operating on the Navi Mumbai-Chipi and Chipi-Navi Mumbai routes.The airport, located in Chipi village in Vengurla taluka of Sindhudurg district, was inaugurated in October 2021 to boost tourism and connectivity in the Konkan region.However, services at the airport had been suspended due to technical hurdles. The resumption of Chipi airport will greatly benefit tourists from Maharashtra and elsewhere, state Ports Minister Nitesh Rane had said..According to a Government Resolution (GR) issued by the General Administration Department on Monday, the funding has been sanctioned to M/s Just Udo Aviation Pvt Ltd (Fly 91) at the rate of Rs 6,200 per seat under the Centre's Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) guidelines.Earlier, on March 30 this year, the government approved Fly 91 to operate flights on the Chipi-Mumbai-Chipi route. However, the airline could not secure slots at the Mumbai airport. Following this, the Maharashtra Airport Development Company (MADC) proposed operating the flights on the Sindhudurg-Navi Mumbai-Sindhudurg route instead.The government has formally cancelled the March 30 approval for the Mumbai route and granted administrative and financial nod to spend Rs 16,74,62,000 for the Sindhudurg-Navi Mumbai sector, the officials said..As per the GR, the 100 percent VGF support will be valid for a period of one year from the date actual flight operations begin, or until the route is formally included and started under the central government's RCS-UDAN scheme, whichever is earlier. No extension will be granted beyond this one-year..Follow PSU Watch on LinkedIN.91% of Mumbai Airport's international traffic to remain unaffected as Terminal 1 is rebuilt.The government has also directed MADC to pursue the inclusion of the Sindhudurg-Navi Mumbai route under the Centre's RCS scheme. Additionally, MADC has been asked to hold discussions with Fly 91 to negotiate a possible reduction in the VGF rate, even though the Request for Proposal does not have a provision for negotiation.The VGF payments will be calculated and disbursed based on the actual frequency of flights operated on the route, the GR stated..(PSU Watch is India's Business News centre that places the spotlight on PSUs, Bureaucracy, Defence and Public Policy. 👉 Click to join our channel now: PSUWatch WhatsApp Channel. Prefer LinkedIn? Follow PSU Watch on LinkedIN. Click to stay connected on Twitter here and stay updated)
